record.paper_title: Measurement of Energy Spectrum and Elemental Composition of PeV Cosmic Rays: Open Problems and Prospects
record.original_question: Which nuclear mass component is responsible for the all-particle cosmic-ray knee observed at about 4 × 10^15 eV: a cutoff of the light proton-plus-helium component at a few PeV, or an all-particle knee dominated by heavier nuclei after the light component has already cut off below about 1 PeV?

evidence.quote: All experiments observed the knee at about 4 × 1015 eV but a general consensus about the chemical component responsible for such a feature does not exist yet because experimental results are still conflicting, as will be discussed in Section 5.

Several experimental results associate the knee with the bending of the light component (p and He), and are compatible with a rigidity-dependent cut-off [22–24,53–55]. However, the flux of the different components vary significantly depending on the interaction model used to interpret the data [22–24]. On the contrary, other results (in particular those obtained by arrays located at high altitudes) seem to indicate that the knee of the all-particle energy spectrum is due to heavier nuclei and that the light component cuts off well below 1 PeV [21,26,31,52,53,56].

The elemental composition is conflicting. Experiments located at high and extreme altitude (BASJE-MAS, Tibet ASγ, ARGO-YBJ, EAS-TOP and CASA-MIA) reported evidence that the knee of the (p+He) component is below 1 PeV and that the composition at the all-particle knee energy is dominated by heavier nuclei. Experiments located deeper in atmosphere (KASCADE, KASCADE-Grande, IceTop/IceCube, Tunka-133) reported evidence that the proton knee is at the same energy of the all-particle knee.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The all-particle cosmic-ray energy spectrum, when multiplied by E^2.7, exhibits a steepening feature known as the "knee" at a primary energy of approximately 4 × 10^15 eV, where the spectral index changes from about -2.7 to about -3.1. Cosmic-ray primaries are nuclei spanning from protons (Z=1, A=1) up to iron-group elements (Z≈26, A≈56), and the flux of each nuclear species is conventionally assumed to cut off at a characteristic energy E_c(Z) that depends on rigidity R = E/Z (a "rigidity-dependent cutoff"). Two competing scenarios have been proposed to explain the all-particle knee:

(i) Light-component scenario: The knee at 4 × 10^15 eV is produced by the cutoff of the combined proton + helium flux at a few PeV, with heavier components cutting off at proportionally higher energies according to rigidity dependence.

(ii) Heavy-component scenario: The proton (and helium) flux already cuts off well below 1 PeV, so that at 4 × 10^15 eV the all-particle flux is dominated by intermediate and heavy nuclei (CNO, Si, Fe groups), and the observed knee is due to the bending of these heavier components.

Problem: Determine which of these two scenarios correctly describes the elemental composition of cosmic rays in the energy range from roughly 10^14 eV to 10^16 eV, and in particular identify the nuclear mass component (light p+He versus heavier nuclei) responsible for the all-particle knee at approximately 4 × 10^15 eV.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is an outstanding open problem in cosmic-ray astrophysics. Experimental results remain conflicting: high-altitude air-shower arrays (Tibet ASγ, ARGO-YBJ, EAS-TOP, CASA-MIA, BASJE-MAS) favor a low-energy (sub-PeV) cutoff of the light component with the all-particle knee dominated by heavier nuclei, while deeper-atmosphere experiments (KASCADE, KASCADE-Grande, IceTop/IceCube, Tunka-133) place the proton/light-component knee at the same energy as the all-particle knee. Recent measurements (e.g., LHAASO, GRAPES-3) continue to address but have not definitively resolved the discrepancy, which is sensitive to the hadronic interaction model used.

status_evidence.title: LHAASO measurement of light-component spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Recent LHAASO results report a knee of the light (p+He) component below 1 PeV, but tensions with other experiments persist.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing experiments continue to probe but have not settled the issue.
